lines.text: Every morning she waves, and every morning you wave back without looking.
lines.say: [warm, close] Every morning she waves, and every morning you wave back without looking.

lines.text: Forty-two.
lines.say: [almost a whisper] Forty-two.

lines.text: So what if you knew the last time you'd see someone?
lines.say: [curious, low] So what if you knew the last time you'd see someone?

lines.text: Mom: Call the minute you reach!
lines.say: [warm, calling out from the door] Call the minute you reach!

lines.text: Tonight you leave for a first job, in a city that doesn't know your name yet.
lines.say: [dry, easy] Tonight you leave for a first job, in a city that doesn't know your name yet.

lines.text: That's forty-two goodbyes left at that door. What would you do with them?
lines.say: [warm, slower] That's forty-two goodbyes left at that door. What would you do with them?

lines.text: Nobody else can see it. Just you.
lines.say: [light, confiding] Nobody else can see it. Just you.

lines.text: Everyone you know has one: the times you'll actually be in the same room again, if your plans stay exactly as they are.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Everyone you know has one: the times you'll actually be in the same room again, if your plans stay exactly as they are.

lines.text: Calls don't count. Only being there.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Calls don't count. Only being there.

lines.text: Change your plans, and it does the maths again.
lines.say: [plain, exact] Change your plans, and it does the maths again.

lines.text: Keep the life you've just signed up for, two trips home a year, and that comes to forty-two.
lines.say: [dry] Keep the life you've just signed up for, two trips home a year, and that comes to forty-two.

lines.text: It's a number. It only counts down.
lines.say: [wry, offhand] It's a number. It only counts down.

lines.text: And she'll be at that door. She always is.
lines.say: [easy, certain] And she'll be at that door. She always is.

lines.text: Next morning, in the new city, the chai-wallah on platform two reads one.
lines.say: [amused] Next morning, in the new city, the chai-wallah on platform two reads one.

lines.text: One last chai, from a man you'll never see again.
lines.say: [softer] One last chai, from a man you'll never see again.

lines.text: And somehow it's the best chai of your life. Station chai.
lines.say: [surprised] And somehow it's the best chai of your life. Station chai.

lines.text: Maybe it isn't the chai.
lines.say: [curious, low] Maybe it isn't the chai.

lines.text: In one taste test, students were told, "This is your last chocolate."
lines.say: [quick, an aside] In one taste test, students were told, "This is your last chocolate."

lines.text: 64% picked it as their favourite, whatever the flavour.
lines.say: [quick, an aside] Sixty-four per cent picked it as their favourite, whatever the flavour.

lines.text: You almost go back for a second glass, but then it wouldn't be the last.
lines.say: [amused] You almost go back for a second glass, but then it wouldn't be the last.

lines.text: On the metro, a total stranger reads four hundred: four hundred mornings with someone you'll never speak to.
lines.say: [puzzled, then dry] On the metro, a total stranger reads four hundred: four hundred mornings with someone you'll never speak to.

lines.text: She's your commute now.
lines.say: [deadpan] She's your commute now.

lines.text: And at the office there's Mehta from Accounts, who reads three thousand.
lines.say: [dry] And at the office there's Mayta from Accounts, who reads three thousand.

lines.text: So you hide.
lines.say: [conspiratorial, quick] So you hide.

lines.text: Mehta: Saved you a seat!
lines.say: [cheerful, too loud] Saved you a seat!

lines.text: Three thousand meetings, and most of them are actual meetings.
lines.say: [deadpan] Three thousand meetings, and most of them are actual meetings.

lines.text: Then comes your first Friday. Go home, or sleep till noon?
lines.say: [teasing] Then comes your first Friday. Go home, or sleep till noon?

lines.text: Home. Obviously.
lines.say: [dry] Home. Obviously.

lines.text: You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.
lines.say: [surprised, quieter] You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.

lines.text: This visit was already counted.
lines.say: [low] This visit was already counted.

lines.text: She's had the chai ready since your train left the city.
lines.say: [warm, fond] She's had the chai ready since your train left the city.

lines.text: And Grandpa reads eight.
lines.say: [warm] And Grandpa reads eight.

lines.text: Grandpa: So there I was, on my bicycle, and the buffalo...
lines.say: [old man, delighted, telling a tale] So there I was, on my bicycle, and the buffalo...

lines.text: You've never once stayed for the end of this story.
lines.say: [fond, wry] You've never once stayed for the end of this story.

lines.text: Grandpa: How does it end?
lines.say: [puzzled, gentle] How does it end?

lines.text: You don't know it either.
lines.say: [dry] You don't know it either.

lines.text: Mom: Next month?
lines.say: [hopeful, soft] Next month?

lines.text: You say, "Let's see. Work."
lines.say: [warm, casual] You say, "Let's see. Work."

lines.text: Thirty-nine. You didn't lose one visit, you lost two.
lines.say: [flat, quiet] Thirty-nine. You didn't lose one visit, you lost two.

lines.text: Because "let's see" was a plan too, and it did the maths.
lines.say: [dry, landing] Because "let's see" was a plan too, and it did the maths.

lines.text: Thirty-nine. Fine. Call it an allowance, and you'll spend it carefully.
lines.say: [wry, half to yourself] Thirty-nine. Fine. Call it an allowance, and you'll spend it carefully.

lines.text: It only counts down. You've watched it.
lines.say: [certain, a little too sure] It only counts down. You've watched it.

lines.text: Then October comes, with Diwali and a deadline in the same week.
lines.say: [brisk] Then October comes, with Diwaali and a deadline in the same week.

lines.text: Thirty-nine is plenty. Skip this one, and save it for later.
lines.say: [breezy] Thirty-nine is plenty. Skip this one, and save it for later.

lines.text: Mom: Look, I lit all of them!
lines.say: [proud, excited, on a phone] Look, I lit all of them!

lines.text: Calls don't count.
lines.say: [flat] Calls don't count.

lines.text: Thirty-eight. You skipped it to save it, and it's just gone.
lines.say: [low, slow] Thirty-eight. You skipped it to save it, and it's just gone.

lines.text: Mehta, meanwhile, is doing fine.
lines.say: [deadpan] Mayta, meanwhile, is doing fine.

lines.text: Thirty-eight visits, a weekend each.
lines.say: [careful, slow] Thirty-eight visits, a weekend each.

lines.text: A writer, Tim Urban, once did this sum on his own guesses.
lines.say: [plain] A writer, Tim Urban, once did this sum on his own guesses.

lines.text: By the time he left school? 93%.
lines.say: [plain] By the time he left school? Ninety-three per cent.

lines.text: Of his time with his parents, in person, already used up.
lines.say: [plain] Of his time with his parents, in person, already used up.

lines.text: Your strip is thinner.
lines.say: [quiet, exact] Your strip is thinner.

lines.text: You're not at the start of your time with her. You're at the tail end.
lines.say: [hushed] You're not at the start of your time with her. You're at the tail end.

lines.text: Then a Friday comes with no festival and no plan. Train, or sleep?
lines.say: [tired] Then a Friday comes with no festival and no plan. Train, or sleep?

lines.text: Train.
lines.say: [quick, decided] Train.

lines.text: Thirty-eight. Here comes the drop.
lines.say: [tense, quiet] Thirty-eight. Here comes the drop.

lines.text: Mom: Next month, then?
lines.say: [teasing, hopeful] Next month, then?

lines.text: You open your mouth to say "let's see".
lines.say: [quick, half-swallowed] You open your mouth to say "let's see".

lines.text: It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, warm] It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.

lines.text: It only counted down because you only ever planned less.
lines.say: [warm, landing] It only counted down because you only ever planned less.

lines.text: But then the offer comes: a bigger job, in a bigger city, on duty every festival.
lines.say: [brisk, tempting] But then the offer comes: a bigger job, in a bigger city, on duty every festival.

lines.text: Nine.
lines.say: [cold, quiet] Nine.

lines.text: The offer, or the Friday train?
lines.say: [low, warm] The offer, or the Friday train?

lines.text: Saying no isn't a plan. A ticket is.
lines.say: [dry, landing] Saying no isn't a plan. A ticket is.

lines.text: Mom: More dal?
lines.say: [warm, laughing] More daal?

lines.text: Grandpa's story? You learned the ending. Well. You made one up.
lines.say: [amused, warm] Grandpa's story? You learned the ending. Well. You made one up.

lines.text: Grandpa: Hah! Yours is better.
lines.say: [old man, laughing, delighted] Hah! Yours is better.

lines.text: Of course she is.
lines.say: [hushed, warm] Of course she is.

lines.text: Whose number would you want to see? Tell us below.
lines.say: [warm, plain] Whose number would you want to see? Tell us below.
